title: Christ speaks inwardly (III.1)
hookLine: blessed is the soul that hears the Lord speaking within
tomorrow: what's the one thing that makes heavy things feel light?

cards: Buzz: a group chat. Buzz: a sale. Buzz: someone liked a photo from last spring.
The loudest things in a day aren't always the ones that matter. The voice that matters, the one that says slow down, or call her back, or you are loved, hardly ever buzzes.
Book three of the Imitation opens on that problem. Until now one voice has been giving counsel. From here on, the book becomes mostly a conversation: the disciple speaks, and Christ answers.

teach.h: I WILL HEAR WHAT THE LORD WILL SPEAK.
teach.b: It begins with a psalm. In the Douay-Rheims: "I will hear what the Lord God will speak in me." Then the blessings.
Blessed is the soul, the chapter says, that hears the Lord speaking within, in the Latin, in se loquentem, and takes from his mouth a word of comfort.

Blessed are the ears that catch God's quiet whisper and pay no attention to the whispering of the world. Blessed are the ears that listen, not to the voice sounding outside, but to the truth teaching within.

teach.h: SHUT THE DOORS OF THE SENSES.
teach.b: So the disciple tells his own soul: shut the doors of your senses for a while, so you can hear what the Lord your God says in you.

And when Christ speaks, his first words are simple: I am your salvation, your peace, your life; stay with me and you'll find peace. Nothing here promises a voice out loud. It's a listening, under the buzz.
Less noise, more ear: that's the whole practice. Now look back at the week, because it led here. Peace first steadied the listener.
Two wings simplified the aim. Above all set the order.
A familiar friend made the talk possible. The cup and the royal way kept the friendship through hard days. Book two taught the inner life.
Book three lets the inner voice speak.

how: Catholics make room to listen in prayer through silent mental prayer, lectio divina, retreats and quiet time before the Blessed Sacrament, and some begin with a line of a psalm.

o: hearing a voice out loud during prayer
listening within for the truth beneath the noise
speaking your own thoughts in God's name

games.q: the inner voice — tap the pairs.

s: Christ speaks inwardly means hearing a voice out loud
the chapter blesses ears that hear the truth teaching within, beneath the world's noise.
book three opens with a line from a psalm
I will hear what the Lord God will speak in me.
the chapter tells readers to shut out every person
it says shut the doors of the senses to listen within, not to shut out people.

games.q: your phone buzzes again and again while a friend is telling you something hard. what does the first chapter of book three point toward?
o: turn it over, and listen to her and to what's under her words.
check it fast in case it's something important.
ask her to text it so you can read it later.
games.why: blessed are the ears, the chapter says, that pay no attention to the whispering of the world. the buzz can wait; the voice in front of you can't.

practice: Turn your phone face down and listen to the room until you can name one sound under the others: a fan, traffic, your own breath.

Stay with it, then listen underneath it, for nothing in particular, the way you'd lean toward a friend across a noisy table. If you pray, begin with the psalm: I will hear what the Lord God will speak in me.

orig.note: Latin, from the Imitation III.1: the soul that hears the Lord speaking within it.

carryVoice: Hold onto this: speaking within, quieter than every buzz and worth the wait. Another week, folded and put away.
